access_mode.description:
The access mode of the disk.
For example:
  * READ_WRITE_SINGLE: The default AccessMode, means the disk can be attached to single instance in RW mode.
  * READ_WRITE_MANY: The AccessMode means the disk can be attached to multiple instances in RW mode.
  * READ_ONLY_SINGLE: The AccessMode means the disk can be attached to multiple instances in RO mode.
The AccessMode is only valid for Hyperdisk disk types.
access_mode.rationale: This changes whether a supported Hyperdisk can be attached to one or several VMs. Disk attachment permissions are still controlled by IAM, and blocking multi-writer mode for every team would break valid clustered workloads.

create_snapshot_before_destroy.description:
If set to true, a snapshot of the disk will be created before it is destroyed.
If your disk is encrypted with customer managed encryption keys these will be reused for the snapshot creation.
The name of the snapshot by default will be '{{disk-name}}-YYYYMMDD-HHmm'
create_snapshot_before_destroy.rationale: This is a Terraform destroy-time backup choice. Requiring a snapshot for every disk could retain data that a team intended to delete, so it is not a safe organisation-wide rule; deletion_policy is the direct control for accidental destruction.

create_snapshot_before_destroy_prefix.description: This will set a custom name prefix for the snapshot that's created when the disk is deleted.
create_snapshot_before_destroy_prefix.rationale: This only changes the generated snapshot name. It does not affect who can access the snapshot or how its data is encrypted.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: DELETE allows the data disk to be destroyed, while ABANDON leaves it outside Terraform management. A platform policy can require PREVENT to reduce accidental or unauthorised data loss.

description.description:
An optional description of this resource. Provide this property when
you create the resource.
description.rationale: This is free-text documentation for the disk and does not change access, encryption, or deletion behaviour.

image.description:
The image from which to initialize this disk. This can be
one of: the image's 'self_link', 'projects/{project}/global/images/{image}',
'projects/{project}/global/images/family/{family}', 'global/images/{image}',
'global/images/family/{family}', 'family/{family}', '{project}/{family}',
'{project}/{image}', '{family}', or '{image}'. If referred by family, the
images names must include the family name. If they don't, use the
[google_compute_image data source](/docs/providers/google/d/compute_image.html).
For instance, the image 'centos-6-v20180104' includes its family name 'centos-6'.
These images can be referred by family name here.
image.rationale: This is a reference to the image used as a source. A useful allowlist would depend on team-specific image projects, while the source image's own controls should be enforced on the image resource.

labels.description:
Labels to apply to this disk.  A list of key->value pairs.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are metadata for organisation and filtering. They do not grant access to the disk or alter its encryption.

licenses.rationale: The license URI records software licensing information. It does not control disk permissions or data protection.

name.description:
Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match
the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the
first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last
character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: The name identifies the disk. Google already validates its format, and changing the name does not change the disk's security behaviour.

physical_block_size_bytes.description:
Physical block size of the persistent disk, in bytes. If not present
in a request, a default value is used. Currently supported sizes
are 4096 and 16384, other sizes may be added in the future.
If an unsupported value is requested, the error message will list
the supported values for the caller's project.
physical_block_size_bytes.rationale: This selects a supported storage block size for compatibility and performance. It does not affect access control or encryption.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This identifies the project that owns the disk. Valid project IDs are team-specific, and access to create or use the disk is already governed by project IAM.

provisioned_iops.description:
Indicates how many IOPS to provision for the disk. This sets the number of I/O operations per second
that the disk can handle. Values must be between 10,000 and 120,000.
For more details, see the Extreme persistent disk [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/extreme-persistent-disk).
provisioned_iops.rationale: This sets disk performance capacity in I/O operations per second. It affects performance and cost, not access or data protection.

provisioned_throughput.description:
Indicates how much throughput to provision for the disk. This sets the number of throughput
mb per second that the disk can handle. Values must be greater than or equal to 1.
provisioned_throughput.rationale: This is a performance setting for disk throughput. A platform security policy has no generally safe throughput value to enforce.

region.description: A reference to the region where the disk resides.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

replica_zones.description: URLs of the zones where the disk should be replicated to.
replica_zones.rationale: The replica zones are selected for availability within the disk's region, and Google validates the allowed placement. Exact zones depend on the workload; the region policy already covers data residency.

size.description:
Size of the persistent disk, specified in GB. You can specify this
field when creating a persistent disk using the sourceImage or
sourceSnapshot parameter, or specify it alone to create an empty
persistent disk.

If you specify this field along with sourceImage or sourceSnapshot,
the value of sizeGb must not be less than the size of the sourceImage
or the size of the snapshot.
size.rationale: Disk size is a capacity and cost decision. It does not change encryption, permissions, or network exposure.

snapshot.description:
The source snapshot used to create this disk. You can provide this as
a partial or full URL to the resource. For example, the following are
valid values:

* 'https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project/global/snapshots/snapshot'
* 'projects/project/global/snapshots/snapshot'
* 'global/snapshots/snapshot'
* 'snapshot'
snapshot.rationale: This is a reference to the snapshot used to populate the disk. The snapshot's access and encryption should be controlled on the snapshot resource rather than by a generic name restriction here.

source_disk.rationale: This points to the disk being cloned. The appropriate source is workload-specific, and security of that disk belongs to the source resource's own policies.

type.description:
URL of the disk type resource describing which disk type to use to
create the disk. Provide this when creating the disk.
type.rationale: The disk type mainly changes storage technology, performance, and cost. Supported disk types are encrypted by Google by default, so there is no universal security value to require.

async_primary_disk.disk.description: Primary disk for asynchronous disk replication.
async_primary_disk.disk.rationale: This is a reference to the primary disk in an asynchronous replication pair. The correct primary is specific to each disaster-recovery design, and its security is enforced on that disk resource.

disk_encryption_key.description:
Encrypts the disk using a customer-supplied encryption key.

After you encrypt a disk with a customer-supplied key, you must
provide the same key if you use the disk later (e.g. to create a disk
snapshot or an image, or to attach the disk to a virtual machine).

Customer-supplied encryption keys do not protect access to metadata of
the disk.

If you do not provide an encryption key when creating the disk, then
the disk will be encrypted using an automatically generated key and
you do not need to provide a key to use the disk later.

disk_encryption_key.kms_key_name.description: The name of the encryption key that is stored in Google Cloud KMS.
disk_encryption_key.kms_key_name.rationale: This selects the Cloud KMS key used to encrypt the new disk. A generic policy can require a non-empty KMS key so the organisation controls key rotation, revocation, and audit logging.

disk_encryption_key.raw_key.description:
Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
disk_encryption_key.raw_key.rationale: A raw customer-supplied key is stored in Terraform configuration and state, creating a direct secret-exposure risk. A platform policy can reject raw_key and require KMS-backed encryption instead.

disk_encryption_key.rsa_encrypted_key.description:
Specifies an RFC 4648 base64 encoded, RSA-wrapped 2048-bit
customer-supplied encryption key to either encrypt or decrypt
this resource. You can provide either the rawKey or the rsaEncryptedKey.
disk_encryption_key.rsa_encrypted_key.rationale: The key material is already RSA-wrapped rather than stored in plaintext. The organisation-wide encryption requirement can be enforced through kms_key_name, so a separate rule on this value adds no general protection.

guest_os_features.description:
A list of features to enable on the guest operating system.
Applicable only for bootable disks.

guest_os_features.type.description: The type of supported feature. Read [Enabling guest operating system features](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/images/create-delete-deprecate-private-images#guest-os-features) to see a list of available options. Possible values: ["MULTI_IP_SUBNET", "SECURE_BOOT", "SEV_CAPABLE", "UEFI_COMPATIBLE", "VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE", "WINDOWS", "GVNIC", "SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE", "SEV_SNP_CAPABLE", "SUSPEND_RESUME_COMPATIBLE", "TDX_CAPABLE", "SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE_V2", "SNP_SVSM_CAPABLE"]
guest_os_features.type.rationale: These values describe guest OS capabilities and compatibility. For example, declaring SECURE_BOOT support does not enable Secure Boot on a VM, and the required features vary by operating system.

source_image_encryption_key.description:
The customer-supplied encryption key of the source image. Required if
the source image is protected by a customer-supplied encryption key.

source_image_encryption_key.kms_key_name.description: The name of the encryption key that is stored in Google Cloud KMS.
source_image_encryption_key.kms_key_name.rationale: This supplies the key reference needed to read an already encrypted source image; it does not choose encryption for the new disk. The valid key is tied to that source image and cannot be constrained generically.

source_image_encryption_key.kms_key_serv.description:
The service account used for the encryption request for the given KMS key.
If absent, the Compute Engine Service Agent service account is used.
source_image_encryption_key.kms_key_serv.rationale: This chooses the identity used to access the source image's KMS key. The correct service account is team-specific, while permission to use the key is enforced by Cloud KMS IAM.

source_image_encryption_key.raw_key.description:
Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
source_image_encryption_key.raw_key.rationale: This places the source image's raw decryption key in Terraform configuration and state. A generic policy can reject raw key use to avoid exposing customer-supplied key material.

source_image_encryption_key.rsa_encrypte.description:
Specifies an RFC 4648 base64 encoded, RSA-wrapped 2048-bit
customer-supplied encryption key to either encrypt or decrypt
this resource. You can provide either the rawKey or the rsaEncryptedKey.
source_image_encryption_key.rsa_encrypte.rationale: This is an RSA-wrapped key used only when a source image already uses that encryption method. It avoids plaintext key material, and requiring or blocking it for every source image would not be a valid general rule.

source_snapshot_encryption_key.description:
The customer-supplied encryption key of the source snapshot. Required
if the source snapshot is protected by a customer-supplied encryption
key.

source_snapshot_encryption_key.raw_key.description:
Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
source_snapshot_encryption_key.raw_key.rationale: This exposes the source snapshot's raw decryption key through Terraform configuration and state. A platform policy can prohibit this field and avoid handling plaintext customer-supplied keys.
